subproblem.title: Difference of two integral flat decompositions (mass subadditivity)
subproblem.statement: Assume LC (as in top_dim_approx). Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and R₁, R₂ ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S₁, S₂ ∈ D_n(U) integer multiplicity. Then there are integer multiplicity R ∈ D_{n+1}(U), S ∈ D_n(U) with ∂R(ω) + S(ω) = (∂R₁(ω) + S₁(ω)) − (∂R₂(ω) + S₂(ω)) for every ω ∈ D^n(U), and M(R) + M(S) ≤ (M(R₁) + M(S₁)) + (M(R₂) + M(S₂)) (M = M_U).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T₁ T₂ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (a b : ℤ), IsIntegerMultiplicity T₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity T₂ → (∀ ω, S ω = (a : ℝ) * T₁ ω + (b : ℝ) * T₂ ω) → IsIntegerMultiplicity S) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (R₁ R₂ : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (S₁ S₂ : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsIntegerMultiplicity R₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity R₂ → IsIntegerMultiplicity S₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity S₂ → ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity S ∧ (∀ ω, R.boundary ω + S ω = (R₁.boundary ω + S₁ ω) - (R₂.boundary ω + S₂ ω)) ∧ R.mass + S.mass ≤ (R₁.mass + S₁.mass) + (R₂.mass + S₂.mass)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 3 ("R := R_i − R_j and S := S_i − S_j are integer multiplicity (sibling im_lincomb with a = 1, b = −1), and M(R) + M(S) ≤ M(R_i) + M(R_j) + M(S_i) + M(S_j) (F2)"). LC is the frozen statement of the parent's sibling fiw_im_lincomb.

1. Difference current. For Z₁, Z₂ ∈ D_k(U), define Z₁ ⊖ Z₂ with underlying linear map Z₁.toCurrent − Z₂.toCurrent. It is sequentially continuous: if TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, then Z₁(ω_j) → 0 and Z₂(ω_j) → 0, so Z₁(ω_j) − Z₂(ω_j) → 0 (Tendsto.sub). So Z₁ ⊖ Z₂ ∈ D_k(U) and (Z₁ ⊖ Z₂)(ω) = Z₁(ω) − Z₂(ω).
2. Put R := R₁ ⊖ R₂ ∈ D_{n+1}(U) and S := S₁ ⊖ S₂ ∈ D_n(U). Since R(ω) = 1·R₁(ω) + (−1)·R₂(ω) for every ω, LC (U open, T₁ := R₁, T₂ := R₂, a := 1, b := −1) shows that R is integer multiplicity; likewise S.
3. Boundary identity. For ω ∈ D^n(U), ∂R(ω) = R(dω) = R₁(dω) − R₂(dω) = ∂R₁(ω) − ∂R₂(ω) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply). Hence ∂R(ω) + S(ω) = (∂R₁(ω) − ∂R₂(ω)) + (S₁(ω) − S₂(ω)) = (∂R₁(ω) + S₁(ω)) − (∂R₂(ω) + S₂(ω)).
4. Mass subadditivity: M(Z₁ ⊖ Z₂) ≤ M(Z₁) + M(Z₂). Let ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U k U. Then −ω is admissible as well (tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω, covectorEuclideanNorm_neg), and Z₂(−ω) = −Z₂(ω). So ofReal(Z₁(ω) − Z₂(ω)) ≤ ofReal(Z₁(ω)) + ofReal(Z₂(−ω)) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le) ≤ M(Z₁) + M(Z₂) (le_massOn twice). Take the supremum (sSup_le).
5. By step 4, M(R) + M(S) ≤ (M(R₁) + M(R₂)) + (M(S₁) + M(S₂)) = (M(R₁) + M(S₁)) + (M(R₂) + M(S₂)) (commutativity and associativity in [0, ∞]). ∎
proof_key_steps: The difference of two sequentially continuous currents is a current.
R := R₁ − R₂ and S := S₁ − S₂ are integer multiplicity by LC with a = 1, b = −1.
∂(R₁ − R₂) = ∂R₁ − ∂R₂, which gives the boundary identity.
M(Z₁ − Z₂) ≤ M(Z₁) + M(Z₂), because −ω is admissible whenever ω is.

subproblem.title: Faces with nonzero coefficient lie in the support, and |β_F|ρ^n ≤ M(P) (G5 a, b)
subproblem.statement: Let m, N ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, ρ > 0, β : LatticeFaceIndex n N → ℝ and Pc ∈ D_n(ℝ^N) with IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc (Pc(ω) = Σ'_F β_F latticeFaceAction ρ F ω for all ω ∈ D^n(ℝ^N)). Then for every face index F with β_F ≠ 0: latticeFace ρ F ⊆ spt Pc, and |β_F| ρ^n ≤ M(Pc), i.e. ENNReal.ofReal(|β_F| ρ^n) ≤ Pc.mass.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ) (β : LatticeFaceIndex (m + 1) N → ℝ) (Pc : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl N)) (m + 1)), 0 < ρ → IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc → ∀ F : LatticeFaceIndex (m + 1) N, β F ≠ 0 → latticeFace ρ F ⊆ Pc.support ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (|β F| * ρ ^ (m + 1)) ≤ Pc.mass
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, preliminary (G5)(a),(b) (lattice chains, parent (P4)); in Simon 7.2 this is the bound Σ|β_F|ρ^n ≤ M(P) used in (2).

Notation. H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N, e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Fix F₀ = (z₀, α₀) with β(F₀) ≠ 0; α₀ : Fin n ↪o Fin N is strictly increasing, A := range α₀. F_0 := latticeFace ρ F₀ = {x : ρz₀_i ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z₀_i + 1) for i ∈ A, x_i = ρz₀_i for i ∉ A} and F̊₀ := {x : ρz₀_i < x_i < ρ(z₀_i + 1) for i ∈ A, x_i = ρz₀_i for i ∉ A}. For p ∈ F̊₀ let d(p) := min_{i ∈ A} min(p_i − ρz₀_i, ρ(z₀_i + 1) − p_i), so 0 < d(p) ≤ ρ/2.

1. Parametrization. Let c₀ ∈ ℝ^N have coordinates ρz₀_i, and ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^N, ι(y) := c₀ + Σ_j y_j e_{α₀(j)}. ι is an isometry (α₀ is injective and (e_i) is orthonormal), ι([0, ρ]^n) = F_0 and ι((0, ρ)^n) = F̊₀. By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, H.map ι = H⌞range ι, and μHE[n] = volume on ℝ^n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence ∫_{F_0} g dH = ∫_{[0,ρ]^n} g(ι(y)) dy for every bounded Borel g, and H(ι(E)) = vol(E) for Borel E ⊆ ℝ^n; in particular H(F_0) = ρ^n. (Lebesgue measure of boxes in ℝ^n = Eucl n: WithLp.ofLp : Eucl n → (Fin n → ℝ) is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp), and Real.volume_Icc_pi gives vol([a, b]^n) = (b − a)^n.)
2. Coordinate covector. Let dx^{α₀} := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (α₀ j)). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, for each strictly increasing α : Fin n → Fin N, dx^{α₀}(e_{α(0)}, …, e_{α(n−1)}) = det[δ_{α₀(i), α(j)}]_{i,j}. This is 1 if α = α₀. If α ≠ α₀ then range α ≠ A (a strictly increasing map out of Fin n is determined by its range), so some α₀(i) ∉ range α, row i of the matrix is zero and the value is 0. Consequently covectorEuclideanNorm(t · dx^{α₀}) = |t| for t ∈ ℝ.
3. Separation of parallel faces. Let p ∈ F̊₀ and 0 < σ ≤ d(p). If F = (z, α₀) ≠ F₀ (so z ≠ z₀), then latticeFace ρ F ∩ ball(p, σ) = ∅. Indeed let x ∈ latticeFace ρ F. If z_i ≠ z₀_i for some i ∉ A, then ‖x − p‖ ≥ |x_i − p_i| = ρ|z_i − z₀_i| ≥ ρ > σ. Otherwise z_i ≠ z₀_i for some i ∈ A. If z_i ≥ z₀_i + 1 then x_i ≥ ρz_i ≥ ρ(z₀_i + 1), so ‖x − p‖ ≥ x_i − p_i ≥ ρ(z₀_i + 1) − p_i ≥ d(p) ≥ σ. If z_i ≤ z₀_i − 1 then x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1) ≤ ρz₀_i, so ‖x − p‖ ≥ p_i − ρz₀_i ≥ σ. In all cases x ∉ ball(p, σ).
4. Evaluation formula. Let O ⊆ ℝ^N be an open set meeting no face (z, α₀) ≠ F₀, ψ : ℝ^N → ℝ smooth with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ O, and ω := ψ • dx^{α₀} (ω(x) = ψ(x) dx^{α₀}), a test n-form on ℝ^N. For F = (z, α) ≠ F₀: if α ≠ α₀, the integrand of latticeFaceAction ρ F ω is ψ(x)·dx^{α₀}(e_{α(0)}, …) = 0 by step 2; if α = α₀, then ψ = 0 on latticeFace ρ F, which is disjoint from O ⊇ tsupport ψ. So latticeFaceAction ρ F ω = 0 for every F ≠ F₀, while latticeFaceAction ρ F₀ ω = ∫_{F_0} ψ dH by step 2. By IsLatticeChain and tsum_eq_single, Pc(ω) = β(F₀) ∫_{F_0} ψ dH.
5. (a), interior points. Suppose p ∈ F̊₀ but p ∉ spt Pc = ℝ^N ∖ zeroRegion(Pc). Then p ∈ W for some open W on which Pc vanishes. Choose σ ∈ (0, d(p)] with ball(p, σ) ⊆ W, and a smooth ψ ≥ 0 with ψ(p) > 0 and tsupport ψ ⊆ ball(p, σ) (exists_contDiff_tsupport_subset applied to ball(p, σ) ∈ 𝓝 p gives a smooth ψ with compact support, tsupport ψ ⊆ ball(p, σ), values in [0, 1] and ψ(p) = 1). By step 3, O := ball(p, σ) meets no other face of direction α₀, so step 4 applies; as tsupport ω ⊆ W, 0 = Pc(ω) = β(F₀) ∫_{F_0} ψ dH. But ∫_{F_0} ψ dH = ∫_{[0,ρ]^n} ψ(ι(y)) dy > 0, because ψ∘ι is continuous and ≥ 0 and is > 0 at ι⁻¹(p) ∈ (0, ρ)^n, hence on a small ball inside [0, ρ]^n of positive Lebesgue measure. Since β(F₀) ≠ 0 this is a contradiction. So F̊₀ ⊆ spt Pc.
6. (a), the closed face. spt Pc is closed (the complement of the open set zeroRegion(Pc)). Every x ∈ F_0 is a limit of points of F̊₀: if c is the centre of F_0 (c ∈ F̊₀), then x + t(c − x) ∈ F̊₀ for t ∈ (0, 1] and x + t(c − x) → x as t → 0⁺. Hence F_0 ⊆ closure(F̊₀) ⊆ spt Pc.
7. (b), the mass bound. For q ≥ 3 let C_q := ι([ρ/q, ρ − ρ/q]^n), a compact subset of F̊₀ with H(C_q) = (ρ(1 − 2/q))^n (step 1), and O_q := thickening(ρ/(2q), C_q), an open set. Every c ∈ C_q has d(c) ≥ ρ/q ≥ ρ/(2q), and every x ∈ O_q lies in ball(c, ρ/(2q)) for some c ∈ C_q; so by step 3, O_q meets no face (z, α₀) ≠ F₀. Smooth Urysohn (exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior with s := C_q and t := cthickening(ρ/(4q), C_q), a compact subset of O_q whose interior contains C_q) gives a smooth ψ_q with 0 ≤ ψ_q ≤ 1, ψ_q = 1 on C_q, and ψ_q = 0 outside t; so tsupport ψ_q ⊆ t is compact and contained in O_q. Let ω_q := sign(β(F₀)) ψ_q • dx^{α₀}. Step 4, applied to sign(β(F₀)) ψ_q, gives Pc(ω_q) = |β(F₀)| ∫_{F_0} ψ_q dH ≥ |β(F₀)| H(C_q), since ψ_q ≥ 0 and ψ_q = 1 on C_q ⊆ F_0. ω_q is admissible for Pc.mass = Pc.massOn univ (tsupport ⊆ univ, and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω_q(x)) = ψ_q(x) ≤ 1 by step 2). So ofReal(|β(F₀)| (ρ(1 − 2/q))^n) ≤ ofReal(Pc(ω_q)) ≤ Pc.mass (le_massOn). As q → ∞, (ρ(1 − 2/q))^n → ρ^n; since ofReal is continuous and {t : ofReal t ≤ Pc.mass} is closed, ofReal(|β(F₀)| ρ^n) ≤ Pc.mass. ∎

Remark (adaptable accepted Lean proof; not needed for the argument above). The measures H(F_0) = ρ^n (step 1) and H(C_q) = (ρ(1 − 2/q))^n (step 7) are instances of the comparator-accepted Submission.isoperimetric_coord_box_measure (commit eefd7c3e7c63582af93eb109b12573ec03d5581a): for α ∈ SimonMultiIndex n N, c : Fin N → ℝ and a ≤ b, μHE[n] {x | ∀ i, (i ∈ range α → c i + a ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ c i + b) ∧ (i ∉ range α → x i = c i)} = ENNReal.ofReal ((b − a)^n). Take c_i := ρ z₀_i with (a, b) := (0, ρ), resp. (ρ/q, ρ − ρ/q). Its Lean proof (the isometry ι of step 1) may be copied under a fresh name.
Further adaptable accepted Lean proofs (optional): Submission.br_latticeFace_setIntegral_eq_cube (commit 0561b355216f4041a30f4aaf2a4b139abdf038ca) rewrites ∫_{latticeFace ρ G} g dμHE[d] as ∫_{[0,ρ]^d} g(Σ_l ρ w_l e_l + Σ_j s_j e_{γ(j)}) ds (step 1). Submission.isoperimetric_lattice_face_cutoff (commit b27494a624bd7cb016c2462cf743040f38ce4183) gives, for δ > 0, a smooth compactly supported φ with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on the shrunken face {ρ(z_i + δ) ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1 − δ) (i ∈ range α), x_i = ρz_i otherwise} and φ = 0 on every face (z', α) with z' ≠ z; with δ := 1/q it can serve as ψ_q in step 7 (it vanishes on all other faces of direction α₀, which is all that step 4 uses).
proof_key_steps: Parametrize the face by an isometry ι of [0, ρ]^n, so H^n on the face is Lebesgue measure and H^n(face) = ρ^n.
The coordinate covector dx^{α₀} pairs to 1 with the face's own frame and to 0 with every other direction.
Small neighbourhoods of points of the relative interior meet no other face of the same direction.
For ω = ψ dx^{α₀} supported there, Pc(ω) = β(F₀) ∫_{F₀} ψ dH^n.
(a) A positive bump forces F̊₀ ⊆ spt Pc, and spt Pc is closed. (b) Cutoffs ψ_q = 1 on C_q ↑ F̊₀ give |β(F₀)| ρ^n ≤ M(Pc).

audit.reason: Coordinate covectors eliminate other directions, while geometric separation eliminates other parallel faces. Thus the isolated evaluation requires no unproved summability assumption. Positive bumps give interior support, closedness on univ gives the whole face, and shrinking-face cutoffs yield the exact coefficient mass bound.

subproblem.title: Finitely many bounded integral coefficient vectors supported in a bounded set (G5 c)
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0, Y ⊆ ℝ^N bounded and A ∈ ℝ. Then the set of all β : LatticeFaceIndex n N → ℝ such that every β_F is an integer and, for every F with β_F ≠ 0, latticeFace ρ F ⊆ Y and |β_F| ≤ A, is finite.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ∀ (Y : Set (Eucl N)), Bornology.IsBounded Y → ∀ A : ℝ, {β : LatticeFaceIndex n N → ℝ | (∀ F, ∃ k : ℤ, β F = k) ∧ ∀ F, β F ≠ 0 → latticeFace ρ F ⊆ Y ∧ |β F| ≤ A}.Finite
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, preliminary (G5)(c) and the finite set 𝓑_ρ of Steps 1–2 (Simon 7.2 proof: "there are only finitely many currents P as in (2)").

1. Faces inside Y. Let 𝓕 := {F : latticeFace ρ F ⊆ Y}. For F = (z, α), the point ρz := (ρ z_i)_i lies in latticeFace ρ F: for i ∈ range α, ρz_i ≤ ρz_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1) because ρ > 0; for i ∉ range α the coordinate equals ρz_i. subproblem.title: Restriction to a smaller open domain: mass bound and integer multiplicity (G4)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ U ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, and Y ∈ D_k(U). Let Y|_W := Y.restrictDomain hWU ∈ D_k(W), so Y|_W(ω) = Y(ω) for ω ∈ D^k(W) ⊆ D^k(U). Then M_W(Y|_W) ≤ M_U(Y) (that is, (Y|_W).mass ≤ Y.mass), and if Y is integer multiplicity in U then Y|_W is integer multiplicity in W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (hWU : W ⊆ U), IsOpen W → ∀ Y : GeometricCurrentOn U k, (Y.restrictDomain hWU).mass ≤ Y.mass ∧ (IsIntegerMultiplicity Y → IsIntegerMultiplicity (Y.restrictDomain hWU))

Source: parent proof, preliminary (G4) (restriction of the deformation outputs to U, parent (P3)), stated for a general open W ⊆ U.

Notation. ι := testFormOnInclusion hWU k : D^k(W) → D^k(U) (same underlying form), so Y|_W(ω) = Y(ιω) (GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply). H := μHE[k]. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.

Part (i): the mass bound.
1. (Y|_W).mass = (Y|_W).massOn W = sSup {ofReal(Y|_W(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn W k W}.
2. Let ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn W k W: tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. The form ιω has the same underlying differential form, so tsupport(ιω) ⊆ W ⊆ U and |ιω(x)| ≤ 1; i.e. ιω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U k U. By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(Y|_W(ω)) = ofReal(Y(ιω)) ≤ Y.massOn U = Y.mass.
3. Taking the supremum (sSup_le), (Y|_W).mass ≤ Y.mass.

Part (ii): integer multiplicity.
4. Let Y be integer multiplicity: IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ, θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M, and Y(η) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(η(x)) dH(x) for η ∈ D^k(U). Put M' := M ∩ W. We show that (M', θ, ξ) witnesses that Y|_W is integer multiplicity in W.
5. Elementary triple conditions. M' ⊆ W. M' is H-null-measurable (M is, and W is open, hence measurable). M' is countably k-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono, M' ⊆ M). θ > 0 and θ ∈ ℕ on M' ⊆ M. If K is compact with K ⊆ W then K ⊆ U, so θ is integrable on M ∩ K and hence on M' ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ K (IntegrableOn.mono_set). ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M' because H⌞M' ≤ H⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono).
6. Locality of weighted approximate tangent spaces. Claim: if x ∈ W, L is a linear subspace and HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L holds, then HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M' θ x L holds. The rank condition finrank L = k is unchanged. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P); choose R > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(0, R) (compact support) and δ > 0 with ball(x, δ) ⊆ W (W open). For 0 < r < δ/R put η_r := blowUpMap x r (η_r(z) = r⁻¹ • (z − x)) and g_r(y) := f(y) θ(x + r • y).
   (a) closedBall(0, R) ∩ η_r(M) = closedBall(0, R) ∩ η_r(M'). '⊇' holds as M' ⊆ M. Conversely, if y = η_r(z) with z ∈ M and ‖y‖ ≤ R, then ‖z − x‖ = r‖y‖ ≤ rR < δ, so z ∈ W, z ∈ M' and y ∈ η_r(M').
   (b) For every set A ⊆ ℝ^P: since g_r vanishes outside the closed, hence measurable, ball B̄ := closedBall(0, R), ∫_{y∈A} g_r dH = ∫ g_r d((H⌞A)⌞B̄) (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero for the measure H⌞A) = ∫ g_r d(H⌞(B̄ ∩ A)) (Measure.restrict_restrict, B̄ measurable).
   (c) By (a) and (b), ∫_{η_r(M)} g_r dH = ∫_{η_r(M')} g_r dH for every r ∈ (0, δ/R). This interval belongs to 𝓝[>] 0, so the two functions of r agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0; since the M-integrals tend to θ(x) ∫_L f dH, so do the M'-integrals (Tendsto.congr'). Since H⌞M' ≤ H⌞M this holds for H⌞M'-a.e. x; moreover H⌞M'-a.e. x lies in M' (ae_restrict_mem₀, M' null-measurable), in particular x ∈ W. For such x, step 6 gives HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M' θ x (span(range τ)) with the same τ. Hence IsRectifiableTriple W k M' θ ξ holds, and θ ∈ ℕ on M'.
8. Representation. Let ω ∈ D^k(W). Then Y|_W(ω) = Y(ιω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH(x). If x ∈ M ∖ M' then x ∉ W ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and the integrand is θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0 (ξ(x) is linear). subproblem.title: L¹ translation estimate for a top-dimensional current with an integrable density
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, X ∈ D_n(ℝ^n) a current on univ, and u : ℝ^n → ℝ Lebesgue-integrable with X(ω) = ∫ u(x) ω(x)(e_1, …, e_n) dx for every ω ∈ D^n(ℝ^n), where e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then for every h ∈ ℝ^n, ∫⁻ |u(x + h) − u(x)| dx ≤ |h| · M(∂X) in [0, ∞], M(∂X) = mass of the m-current ∂X on ℝ^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (m + 1)) (u : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ), Integrable u → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (m + 1), X ω = ∫ x, u x * (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) (m + 1)) x (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ))) → ∀ h : Eucl (m + 1), ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal |u (x + h) - u x| ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ‖h‖ * X.boundary.mass
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 2(b) (translation estimate, used for the summed form of Simon 5.1 (32)).

Notation. L := volume (Lebesgue measure) on ℝ^n; e := (e_0, …, e_m) the standard frame; for an n-form η, η_e(x) := η(x)(e). |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α. Λ := M(∂X) = (∂X).massOn univ ∈ [0, ∞].

0. Trivial cases. If h = 0 the left side is ∫⁻ 0 = 0. If h ≠ 0 and Λ = ∞ the right side is ∞. Assume from now on Λ < ∞; write Λ also for its real value. Put w(x) := u(x + h) − u(x); w ∈ L¹(L) (translation invariance of L) and the goal is ∫|w| dL ≤ |h| Λ.
1. Mass bound for a test form (F3). If Z ∈ D_m(ℝ^n), η ∈ D^m(ℝ^n), c > 0 and |η(x)| ≤ c for all x, then |Z(η)| ≤ c·M(Z) (when M(Z) < ∞). First, homogeneity: for t ∈ ℝ and a covector α, covectorEuclideanNorm(t•α) = |t|·covectorEuclideanNorm(α), because (t•α)(e_I)² = t²·α(e_I)² for every I, so the sum under the square root is multiplied by t², and √(t²·s) = |t|·√s (this identity is not in the library and must be proved, which takes two lines). Then c⁻¹η and −c⁻¹η are admissible for M(Z) = Z.massOn univ (tsupport ⊆ univ, |±c⁻¹η(x)| = c⁻¹|η(x)| ≤ 1). By le_massOn, ofReal(c⁻¹Z(η)) ≤ M(Z) and ofReal(−c⁻¹Z(η)) ≤ M(Z), hence |Z(η)| ≤ c M(Z).
2. Divergence forms.    (a) By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^{(k)}(e_{i.succAbove 0}, …, e_{i.succAbove (m−1)}) = det[δ_{k.succAbove a, i.succAbove b}]_{a,b}, which is 1 if k = i and 0 if k ≠ i (then the row a with k.succAbove a = i is zero, as i is not in the range of i.succAbove). Hence ω_G(x)(e ∘ i.succAbove) = (−1)^i G^i(x).
   (b) The strictly increasing maps Fin m → Fin n are exactly the maps i.succAbove (i ∈ Fin n), each obtained once. Indeed, a strictly increasing I : Fin m → Fin (m+1) is not surjective (cardinality), so pick k ∉ range I; then range I ⊆ {k}ᶜ = range k.succAbove (Fin.range_succAbove), both ranges have m elements (injectivity), so they are equal, and two strictly increasing maps with the same range are equal (StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT). Conversely each k.succAbove is strictly increasing (Fin.strictMono_succAbove), and k ↦ k.succAbove is injective (Fin.succAbove_left_injective). So, by the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm, |ω_G(x)| = (Σ_i G^i(x)²)^{1/2} = ‖G(x)‖.
   (c) ω_G is smooth with compact support, so ω_G ∈ D^m(ℝ^n).
   (d) By exteriorDerivative_apply (extDeriv_apply), dω_G(x)(e) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i D[y ↦ ω_G(y)(i.removeNth e)](x)(e_i), and i.removeNth e = e ∘ i.succAbove. By (a), ω_G(y)(i.removeNth e) = (−1)^i G^i(y), so dω_G(x)(e) = Σ_i ∂_i G^i(x) = div G(x).
   (e) By the hypothesis applied to the test form dω_G (= exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ω_G), and by GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply: ∫ u div G dL = X(dω_G) = (∂X)(ω_G). By step 1 and (b): if c > 0 and ‖G(x)‖ ≤ c for all x, then |ω_G(x)| ≤ c for all x and |∫ u div G dL| ≤ c Λ.

For each y, t ↦ g(y − th) is C¹ with derivative −Dg(y − th)(h), so g(y − h) − g(y) = −∫_0^1 Dg(y − th)(h) dt (fundamental theorem of calculus). The function (y, t) ↦ u(y) Dg(y − th)(h) is measurable and bounded by |u(y)| sup‖Dg‖ ‖h‖, hence integrable on ℝ^n × [0, 1]; by Fubini, ∫ w g = −∫_0^1 (∫ u(y) Dg(y − th)(h) dy) dt. For fixed t put G_t(y) := g(y − th) h, a smooth compactly supported vector field with div G_t(y) = Σ_i h_i ∂_i g(y − th) = Dg(y − th)(h) and ‖G_t(y)‖ = |g(y − th)| ‖h‖ ≤ ‖h‖. By step 2(e) with c := ‖h‖ > 0 (h ≠ 0 by step 0), |∫ u(y) Dg(y − th)(h) dy| ≤ ‖h‖ Λ for every t, so |∫ w g| ≤ ∫_0^1 ‖h‖ Λ dt = ‖h‖ Λ.

Replacing O^± by O^± ∩ thickening(δ, K^±), which is still open, contains K^± and satisfies ν(O^± ∖ K^±) < ε, we may assume O⁺ ∩ O⁻ = ∅.
   (c) By IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open there is r > 0 with L^± := cthickening(r, K^±) ⊆ O^±. L^± is compact (closed and bounded in Eucl n), and K^± ⊆ thickening(r, K^±) ⊆ interior L^±. Smooth Urysohn (exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior with model 𝓘(ℝ, Eucl n), s := K^± (closed), t := L^±; ContMDiff for this model is ContDiff ℝ ∞) gives smooth g^± with values in [0, 1], g^± = 1 on K^± and g^± = 0 outside L^±. Hence tsupport g^± ⊆ L^± (L^± is closed) and g^± has compact support.

   (e) Since w = w̃ a.e., ∫ w g dL = ∫ w̃ g dL (all integrals here are finite: w ∈ L¹ and |g| ≤ 1). subproblem.title: Vanishing of a current on test forms supported off its support (G1)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, T ∈ D_n(U) a current (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ D^n(U) a test form (TestFormOn U n). If tsupport ω is disjoint from spt T (T.support = U ∖ zeroRegion(T), Simon Ch. 6, 2.11), then T(ω) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)) T.support → T ω = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, preliminary (G1) ("Support vanishing"); Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (spt T is the complement of the largest open set on which T vanishes).

Notation. T vanishes on W (T.VanishesOn W) if T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W. zeroRegion(T) := ⋃{W : W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, T vanishes on W}, and spt T := U ∖ zeroRegion(T).

1. Put C := tsupport ω. Since ω ∈ D^n(U), ω is smooth, has compact support, and C ⊆ U. In particular C is compact (and closed).
2. C ⊆ zeroRegion(T): if x ∈ C then x ∈ U, and x ∉ spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T) by the disjointness hypothesis; hence x ∈ zeroRegion(T).
3. zeroRegion(T) is the union of the open sets W of the family above, and T vanishes on each of them. By compactness of C there are finitely many members W_1, …, W_N of the family (N ∈ ℕ, possibly N = 0) with C ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_N.
4. Smooth partition of unity. Apply SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate on the manifold ℝ^P with model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), index type Fin N, the closed set C and the open cover (W_i)_{i} of C. It gives smooth functions ψ_1, …, ψ_N : ℝ^P → ℝ (ContMDiff for the model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) is ContDiff ℝ ∞) with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for all i and Σ_i ψ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ C.
5. For each i put η_i := ψ_i • ω, i.e. η_i(x) = ψ_i(x) ω(x). Then η_i is smooth (product of a smooth scalar function and a smooth form), tsupport η_i ⊆ tsupport ω = C is compact, tsupport η_i ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i, and tsupport η_i ⊆ C ⊆ U. Hence η_i ∈ D^n(U), and since T vanishes on W_i, T(η_i) = 0.
6. ω = Σ_i η_i. If x ∈ C then Σ_i η_i(x) = (Σ_i ψ_i(x)) ω(x) = ω(x). If x ∉ C then x ∉ support ω, so ω(x) = 0 and each η_i(x) = ψ_i(x)·0 = 0. Hence the underlying forms agree everywhere, and ω = Σ_i η_i in the submodule D^n(U) (Subtype.ext and funext; for N = 0 this reads ω = 0).
7. By linearity of the underlying linear map of T, T(ω) = Σ_i T(η_i) = 0. ∎

Remark (adaptable accepted Lean proof; not needed for the argument above). The identical frozen type is already comparator-accepted in another branch as Submission.isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support (DAG node root.isoperimetric-a1.vanish_off_support-a1; commit 3ccbe082e5193a06d9f4daa1ada94e9f6aaa7fa6, file GMT/Ch06/Submission.lean, branch humanize-recursive/gmt-ch06/20261011t144224z-6e4735dbca/root-isoperimetric-a1-vanish-off-support-a1-a1). That Lean proof follows steps 1–7 (IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover, SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate with contMDiff_iff_contDiff, Subtype.ext with Finset.sum_smul, map_sum) and can be reused verbatim under the name fiw_tb_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support.

Finitely many open sets W_i on which T vanishes cover tsupport ω.
A smooth partition of unity ψ_i subordinate to (W_i) with Σψ_i = 1 on tsupport ω.
ω = Σ ψ_i ω with each ψ_i ω ∈ D^n(U) supported in W_i, so T(ψ_i ω) = 0.
Linearity gives T(ω) = 0.

subproblem.title: The carrier of a rectifiable current is H^n-null off its support (G2)
subproblem.statement: Assume the mass formula MF: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ D_n(U) and every rectifiable triple (M, θ, ξ) in U (IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ) with T(ω) = ∫_M θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n (tauAction n M θ ξ ω) for all ω ∈ D^n(U), and every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = ∫⁻_{M∩W} θ dH^n (H^n = μHE[n]). subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → ∀ W : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = ∫⁻ x in M ∩ W, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M \ T.support) = 0

Source: parent proof, preliminary (G2), first assertion ("H(M ∖ spt X) = 0"), with (F4) = the hypothesis MF (the frozen statement of the parent's sibling fiw_im_mass_formula) and (G1) = the sibling vanish_off_support.

Notation. H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P. Z := zeroRegion(T), an open set (a union of open sets). spt T = U ∖ Z.

1. Let V := U ∩ Z; V is open because U and Z are open. Since M ⊆ U (IsRectifiableTriple.subset), M ∖ spt T = M ∖ (U ∖ Z) = M ∩ Z = M ∩ V.
2. M_V(T) = 0. By definition T.massOn V = sSup {ofReal(T ω) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n V}. If ω is admissible then tsupport ω ⊆ V ⊆ Z, and Z is disjoint from spt T = U ∖ Z; so tsupport ω and spt T are disjoint and T(ω) = 0 by the sibling vanish_off_support. Thus every element of the set equals ofReal 0 = 0, and the supremum is 0 (sSup_le).
3. Apply MF with these P, n, U (open), T, the triple (M, θ, ξ) and the hypothesis T = τ(M, θ, ξ) on D^n(U), and with the open set W := V. It gives ∫⁻_{M∩V} ofReal(θ x) dH(x) = T.massOn V = 0.
4. Exhaust U by compact sets: there are compact sets K_k ⊆ U (k ∈ ℕ) with ⋃_k K_k = U. (For instance K_k := closedBall(0, k) if U = ℝ^P, and otherwise K_k := {x : ‖x‖ ≤ k and infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/(k+1)}, which is closed and bounded, hence compact, and contained in U; every x ∈ U has positive distance to the closed set ℝ^P ∖ U, so it lies in some K_k.) Put S_k := M ∩ V ∩ K_k.
5. Fix k. K_k is a compact subset of U, so by IsRectifiableTriple.integrableOn θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K_k; in particular θ, and hence x ↦ ofReal(θ x), is a.e.-measurable for H⌞S_k (S_k ⊆ M ∩ K_k). By monotonicity of the lower integral in the set (lintegral_mono_set), ∫⁻_{S_k} ofReal θ dH ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩V} ofReal θ dH = 0. By lintegral_eq_zero_iff', ofReal(θ x) = 0 for H⌞S_k-a.e. x. But θ > 0 on M (IsRectifiableTriple.pos), so ofReal(θ x) ≠ 0 for every x ∈ S_k; hence S_k ⊆ {x : ofReal(θ x) ≠ 0}, which has H⌞S_k-measure 0, and H(S_k) = (H⌞S_k)(S_k) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply_self and monotonicity).
6. M ∩ V ⊆ U = ⋃_k K_k, so M ∩ V = ⋃_k S_k and H(M ∩ V) ≤ Σ_k H(S_k) = 0 (measure_iUnion_null). By step 1, H(M ∖ spt T) = 0. ∎

On each piece S_k = M ∩ V ∩ K_k of a compact exhaustion of U, θ is a.e.-measurable and positive, so H^n(S_k) = 0.
Countable subadditivity gives H^n(M ∖ spt T) = H^n(M ∩ V) = 0.

Every library fact cited below is available under the imports of GMT.Ch06.Submission.

Notation. Currents on ℝ^P are currents on univ. ι := testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) q : D^q(U) → D^q(ℝ^P) (same underlying form). 1. Cutoff. K is compact, U open, and ℝ^P is locally compact Hausdorff, so there is a compact L with K ⊆ interior L and L ⊆ U (exists_compact_between). K is closed. Smooth Urysohn (exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior with model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), smoothness ∞, s := K (closed), t := L, using K ⊆ interior L) gives a smooth χ : ℝ^P → ℝ together with, in this order: (∀ᶠ x in 𝓝ˢ K, χ x = 1), (∀ x ∉ L, χ x = 0) and (∀ x, χ x ∈ [0, 1]). By mem_nhdsSet_iff_exists, the first gives an open set N ⊇ K with χ = 1 on N. (ContMDiff for the model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) is ContDiff ℝ ∞; in Lean write the smoothness exponent as ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞).) Since L is closed and contains support χ, tsupport χ ⊆ L, so tsupport χ is compact and contained in U. Also {x : χ(x) ≠ 1} ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N, a closed set; hence tsupport(1 − χ) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N, which is disjoint from K.
2. Products with χ. For every test q-form ω on ℝ^P, χ•ω (x ↦ χ(x)ω(x)) is smooth and tsupport(χ•ω) ⊆ tsupport χ ∩ tsupport ω; hence χ•ω ∈ D^q(U), and m_χ : D^q(ℝ^P) → D^q(U), ω ↦ χ•ω, is linear. For a test form ω on ℝ^P or on U, (1 − χ)•ω = ω − χ•ω is a test form on the same domain with tsupport((1 − χ)•ω) ⊆ tsupport(1 − χ) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N, which is disjoint from K. Finally |χ(x)ω(x)| = χ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ |ω(x)|. (Compact support of x ↦ g(x) • ω(x) is best obtained from IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset with tsupport_smul_subset_right rather than HasCompactSupport.smul_left.)
3. Vanishing fact (V). If Z is a q-current on ℝ^P (resp. on U) with spt Z ⊆ K and ω is a test q-form on ℝ^P (resp. on U), then Z((1 − χ)•ω) = 0 by the sibling vanish_off_support, because tsupport((1 − χ)•ω) is disjoint from K ⊇ spt Z. Hence Z(ω) = Z(χ•ω) by linearity.
4. Definition of Y and its continuity. For ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) put Y(ω) := X(m_χ ω); Y is linear because m_χ and X are. Put μ_X := M(X).toReal, a real number because M(X) < ∞. Sequential continuity (as required by GeometricCurrentOn) follows from the finite mass of X:
   (a) Evaluation bound (parent fact F3). If η ∈ D^{m+1}(U), c > 0 and |η(x)| ≤ c for every x, then |X(η)| ≤ c·μ_X. Indeed |tα| = |t|·|α| for t ∈ ℝ (each squared coefficient α(e_I)² in the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm is multiplied by t², and √(t²s) = |t|√s), so c⁻¹η and −c⁻¹η lie in massAdmissibleOn U (m+1) U (tsupport ⊆ U, coefficient norm ≤ 1). By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(c⁻¹X(η)) ≤ M(X) and ofReal(−c⁻¹X(η)) = ofReal(X(−c⁻¹η)) ≤ M(X); since M(X) ≠ ∞, ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal gives ±c⁻¹X(η) ≤ μ_X, i.e. |X(η)| ≤ c·μ_X.
   (b) Coefficient norm versus operator norm. Every α ∈ Covector(ℝ^P)(m+1) satisfies |α| ≤ A₀‖α‖, where ‖α‖ is the operator norm of the continuous alternating map α and A₀ := √(P^{m+1}). Indeed, for I : Fin (m+1) → Fin P, ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm and ‖EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i‖ = 1 give |α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(m)})| ≤ ‖α‖; the sum defining |α|² has card(Fin (m+1) → Fin P) = P^{m+1} terms, each ≤ ‖α‖², so |α| ≤ √(P^{m+1}·‖α‖²) = A₀‖α‖.
   (c) Let ω_j → 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges on univ: there is a compact K' with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K' for every j, and (taking k = 0) iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 = 0 uniformly on K'. As ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), for every ε > 0 there is j₀ with ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε for all j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ K'; for x ∉ K', ω_j(x) = 0. Hence, for j ≥ j₀ and every x, |χ(x)ω_j(x)| = χ(x)|ω_j(x)| ≤ A₀ε, by (b) and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1.
   (d) By (a) with η := m_χ ω_j ∈ D^{m+1}(U) and c := (A₀ + 1)ε > 0, |Y(ω_j)| = |X(m_χ ω_j)| ≤ (A₀ + 1)ε·μ_X for all j ≥ j₀. As ε > 0 is arbitrary, Y(ω_j) → 0. Thus Y ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P).
5. Y|_U = X. For ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U): Y(ιω) = X(χ•ω) (the χ•ω's agree as elements of D^{m+1}(U)), and X(ω) = X(χ•ω) by (V) applied to X (spt X ⊆ K). By GeometricCurrentOn.ext, Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) = X.
6. spt Y ⊆ K. Let x ∉ K. As K is closed there is r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ∩ K = ∅. W := ball(x, r) is open, its closure lies in the compact set closedBall(x, r) (so it is compact) and in ℝ^P. If ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport(χ•ω) ⊆ W is disjoint from K ⊇ spt X, so Y(ω) = X(χ•ω) = 0 by vanish_off_support. Hence Y vanishes on W, x ∈ zeroRegion(Y) and x ∉ spt Y = ℝ^P ∖ zeroRegion(Y).
7. Boundary relations. (a) (∂Y)|_U = ∂X: for ω ∈ D^m(U), (∂Y)(ιω) = Y(d(ιω)), and d(ιω) = ι(dω) (both have the underlying form dω), so (∂Y)(ιω) = Y(ι(dω)) = X(dω) = (∂X)(ω) by step 5; conclude with GeometricCurrentOn.ext. (b) spt ∂Y ⊆ spt Y ⊆ K: if Y vanishes on an open W then so does ∂Y, since tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset) gives ∂Y(ω) = Y(dω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W; hence zeroRegion(Y) ⊆ zeroRegion(∂Y).
8. Lemma A (mass). If Z ∈ D_q(ℝ^P) and spt Z ⊆ K, then M(Z) ≤ M(Z|_U). Proof: let ω be admissible for M(Z) = Z.massOn univ (ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P) with |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By (V), Z(ω) = Z(χ•ω) = Z(ι(m_χ ω)) = Z|_U(m_χ ω), and m_χ ω is admissible for M(Z|_U) = (Z|_U).massOn U (tsupport ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ U, and |χ(x)ω(x)| ≤ 1). So ofReal(Z(ω)) ≤ M(Z|_U) by le_massOn; take the supremum.
   Lemma A for Z := Y (q = m + 1) and step 5 give M(Y) ≤ M(X). Lemma A for Z := ∂Y (q = m; spt ∂Y ⊆ K by 7(b)) and 7(a) give M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂X).
9. Lemma B (integrality). If Z ∈ D_q(ℝ^P), spt Z ⊆ K and Z|_U is integer multiplicity in U, then Z is integer multiplicity in ℝ^P. Proof:
   (B1) spt(Z|_U) ⊆ K. By definition spt(Z|_U) ⊆ U. Let x ∈ U ∖ K. U ∖ K is open, so there is r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ⊆ U ∖ K, and W := ball(x, r) is open with compact closure contained in U. If ω ∈ D^q(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport(ιω) ⊆ W is disjoint from K ⊇ spt Z, so Z|_U(ω) = Z(ιω) = 0 (vanish_off_support). So x ∈ zeroRegion(Z|_U) and x ∉ spt(Z|_U).
   (B2) Write Z|_U = τ(M, θ, ξ) with IsRectifiableTriple U q M θ ξ and θ ∈ ℕ on M. By the sibling support_null (with MF; U open), H^q(M ∖ spt(Z|_U)) = 0, hence H^q(M ∖ K) = 0 by (B1). Put M' := M ∩ K. Then M' ⊆ M and H^q(M ∖ M') = 0, so M and M' are H^q-a.e. equal and H^q⌞M = H^q⌞M' (Measure.restrict_congr_set).
   (B3) Blow-ups preserve null sets. For x ∈ ℝ^P, r > 0 and any set E, blowUpMap x r '' E = r⁻¹ • (E − x): translation by −x is an isometry and multiplication by r⁻¹ multiplies H^q by r^{−q} (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). So H^q(blowUpMap x r '' (M ∖ M')) = 0, and since blowUpMap x r '' M' ⊆ blowUpMap x r '' M ⊆ blowUpMap x r '' M' ∪ blowUpMap x r '' (M ∖ M'), the two blown-up sets are H^q-a.e. equal; their restricted measures agree. Hence for every x, every linear subspace L and every f ∈ C_c, the blow-up integrals of (M, θ) and (M', θ) at x coincide for every r > 0, and HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt q M θ x L holds iff HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt q M' θ x L holds.
   (B4) (M', θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity rectifiable triple in ℝ^P (= univ): M' ⊆ univ; M' is null-measurable (M is, K is closed); M' is countably q-rectifiable (subset of M); θ > 0 and θ ∈ ℕ on M'; for every compact K'', M' ∩ K'' ⊆ M ∩ K and θ is integrable on M ∩ K because K is a compact subset of U, so θ is integrable on M' ∩ K''; ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^q⌞M' = H^q⌞M; the orientation condition holds H^q⌞M'-a.e. because it holds H^q⌞M-a.e. for (M, θ) and, by (B3), the same orthonormal τ works for (M', θ).
   (B5) Representation. For ω ∈ D^q(ℝ^P), by (V), Z(ω) = Z(χ•ω) = Z|_U(m_χ ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(χ(x)ω(x)) dH^q = ∫_{M'} θ(x) ξ(x)(χ(x)ω(x)) dH^q (as H^q⌞M = H^q⌞M') = ∫_{M'} θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^q (χ = 1 on K ⊇ M' and ξ(x) is linear; since M' is only null-measurable use setIntegral_congr_fun₀). So Z = τ(M', θ, ξ) on D^q(ℝ^P), and Z is integer multiplicity.
   Lemma B for Z := Y (Y|_U = X): if X is integer multiplicity, so is Y. Lemma B for Z := ∂Y (spt ∂Y ⊆ K and (∂Y)|_U = ∂X by step 7): if ∂X is integer multiplicity, so is ∂Y.
10. Steps 5, 6, 8 and 9 give all the asserted properties of Y. ∎

subproblem.title: Approximation by an integral cubical chain in top dimension P = m + 1 (Simon 5.1, (27)–(37))
subproblem.statement: Assume MF (as in support_null) and LC: for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, all integer multiplicity T₁, T₂ ∈ D_n(U), integers a, b and S ∈ D_n(U) with S(ω) = aT₁(ω) + bT₂(ω) for every ω, S is integer multiplicity. Let m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Then there is c ∈ [0, ∞) such that for every integer multiplicity X ∈ D_n(ℝ^n) with M(X) < ∞ and M(∂X) < ∞ and every ρ > 0 there are β : LatticeFaceIndex n n → ℝ and Pc, S ∈ D_n(ℝ^n) with: IsLatticeChain ρ β Pc; every β_F an integer; β_F ≠ 0 ⟹ latticeFace ρ F ⊆ cthickening(√n ρ, spt X); |β_F| ρ^n ≤ 2 M(X) for every F; S integer multiplicity; X(ω) − Pc(ω) = S(ω) for every ω; and M(S) ≤ c ρ M(∂X).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step 2 (a), (c)–(f), i.e. the printed steps (27)–(37) of the proof of Simon 5.1 with Q := X and R := 0, the cubewise Poincaré inequality (32) being used in summed form via the sibling translation_estimate. MF and LC are the frozen statements of the parent's siblings fiw_im_mass_formula and fiw_im_lincomb. Uses the siblings support_null and translation_estimate.

Notation and constants. n = m + 1; ℝ^n = Eucl n; L := volume = μHE[n] on ℝ^n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). e := (e_0, …, e_m), e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, and η_e(x) := η(x)(e) for an n-form η. Put c := (2√n)^n √n ∈ [0, ∞), which depends only on m. The only order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin n is the identity (it is strictly monotone, hence injective, hence surjective since Fin n is finite, hence an order isomorphism Fin n ≃o Fin n, and that type is a subsingleton; this is not an instance and must be proved), so every face index is F = (z, id) with z ∈ ℤ^n. Write F_z := latticeFace ρ (z, id) = ρ(z + [0, 1]^n) (closed cube) and F̊_z := ρ(z + (0, 1)^n) (open cube). Then latticeFaceAction ρ (z, id) η = ∫_{F_z} η_e dL. The open cubes are pairwise disjoint, ℝ^n ∖ ⋃_z F̊_z ⊆ ⋃_{i,k} {x_i = ρk} is L-null, L(F_z) = ρ^n, L(F_z ∖ F̊_z) = 0 and diam F_z = √n ρ. (Volumes of coordinate boxes in Eucl n are computed with the measure-preserving map WithLp.ofLp : Eucl n → (Fin n → ℝ) (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) and Real.volume_Icc_pi; a coordinate hyperplane {x_i = c} is L-null because its image is a product set with the null factor {c}.) For α ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^n), covectorEuclideanNorm α = |α(e)| (the sum in its definition has the single term I = id).

Fix an integer multiplicity X with M(X) < ∞, Λ := M(∂X) < ∞, and ρ > 0.
1. Density ((27)–(28)). Write X = τ(M, θ, ξ) with IsRectifiableTriple univ n M θ ξ and θ ∈ ℕ on M. Let e* := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj j), so e*(e) = 1. Every alternating n-form α on ℝ^n satisfies α(v) = det[v] α(e), where det[v] is the determinant of the coordinate matrix of v (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det for the standard basis), and an orthonormal frame τ of ℝ^n has det[τ] = ±1 (its matrix Q satisfies QᵀQ = I). So for L-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ(x) gives ξ(x)(α) = ε(x) α(e) for all α, where ε(x) := ξ(x)(e*) ∈ {−1, 1}. Define u(x) := ξ(x)(e*) θ(x) for x ∈ M and u(x) := 0 otherwise. θ is a.e.-measurable for L⌞M: by IsRectifiableTriple.integrableOn it is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on each M ∩ closedBall(0, k), and M = ⋃_k M ∩ closedBall(0, k). Hence u is a.e.-strongly measurable (ξ and θ are, and M is null-measurable), u takes integer values a.e., and |u| = θ·1_M a.e. Replace u by a Borel representative that is integer-valued everywhere: ũ := Int.cast ∘ round ∘ u₀, where u₀ is a strongly measurable modification of u (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk); ũ = u a.e. because u is integer-valued a.e. All integrals below are unchanged; from now on write u for ũ, so every set {u ≤ k} is measurable and u(x) ∈ ℤ for every x. By MF with U = W = univ, M(X) = ∫⁻_M ofReal θ dL = ∫⁻ ofReal|u| dL < ∞, so u ∈ L¹(L). For every ω ∈ D^n(ℝ^n), X(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dL = ∫ u ω_e dL. By the sibling support_null (with MF, U = univ), L(M ∖ spt X) = 0; since u = 0 a.e. off M, u = 0 a.e. outside spt X.
2. Translation estimate. By the sibling translation_estimate applied to X and u: ∫ |u(x + h) − u(x)| dx ≤ ‖h‖ Λ for every h ∈ ℝ^n.
3. Integer medians ((31), (35)). Fix z ∈ ℤ^n and let a_z(k) := L(F_z ∩ {u ≤ k}) for k ∈ ℤ. a_z is nondecreasing, a_z(k) → ρ^n as k → ∞ and a_z(k) → 0 as k → −∞ (continuity of the finite measure L⌞F_z; u is real-valued). So the set {k ∈ ℤ : a_z(k) ≥ ρ^n/2} is nonempty and bounded below; let β_z be its least element. Then (i) L(F_z ∩ {u ≤ β_z}) ≥ ρ^n/2, and (ii) L(F_z ∩ {u ≤ β_z − 1}) < ρ^n/2, hence, as u is integer-valued, L(F_z ∩ {u ≥ β_z}) = ρ^n − L(F_z ∩ {u ≤ β_z − 1}) > ρ^n/2. Consequences:
   (M1) |β_z| ρ^n ≤ 2 ∫_{F_z} |u| dL: if β_z ≥ 1 then |u| ≥ β_z on F_z ∩ {u ≥ β_z}, of measure > ρ^n/2; if β_z ≤ −1 then |u| ≥ |β_z| on F_z ∩ {u ≤ β_z}, of measure ≥ ρ^n/2; if β_z = 0 there is nothing to prove.
   (M2) If β_z ≠ 0 then L(F_z ∩ {u ≠ 0}) > 0: otherwise u = 0 a.e. on F_z, so a_z(0) = ρ^n ≥ ρ^n/2 and a_z(−1) = 0 < ρ^n/2, which gives β_z = 0.
